title: Phantom Order Update
concept: Repositories must not hand out their own mutable state
symptom: OrderService.add_item rejects an item that pushes the order over the limit and raises InvalidOrder. But when you read the order back, the rejected item is in it, as if the update had half happened.
failingTest:
import unittest

from models import LineItem, Order
from repository import InMemoryOrderRepository
from service import InvalidOrder, OrderService


class Failing(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_rejected_item_is_not_left_in_the_saved_order(self):
        repo = InMemoryOrderRepository()
        repo.save(Order("o-1", [LineItem("book", 4000)]))
        service = OrderService(repo)
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidOrder):
            service.add_item("o-1", LineItem("piano", 99_000))
        self.assertEqual([i.sku for i in repo.get("o-1").items], ["book"])
regressionTests:
import unittest

from models import LineItem, Order
from repository import InMemoryOrderRepository, OrderNotFound
from service import InvalidOrder, OrderService


class Regression(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.repo = InMemoryOrderRepository()
        self.repo.save(Order("o-1", [LineItem("book", 4000, 2)]))
        self.service = OrderService(self.repo)

    def test_an_accepted_item_is_saved(self):
        self.service.add_item("o-1", LineItem("pen", 150))
        self.assertEqual([i.sku for i in self.repo.get("o-1").items], ["book", "pen"])
        self.assertEqual(self.repo.get("o-1").total_cents, 8150)

    def test_an_accepted_discount_is_saved(self):
        self.service.apply_discount("o-1", 500)
        self.assertEqual(self.repo.get("o-1").discount_cents, 500)

    def test_a_rejected_discount_leaves_the_saved_discount_alone(self):
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidOrder):
            self.service.apply_discount("o-1", 9_999_999)
        self.assertEqual(self.repo.get("o-1").discount_cents, 0)

    def test_changing_an_order_after_saving_it_does_not_change_the_saved_copy(self):
        order = Order("o-2", [LineItem("lamp", 2500)])
        self.repo.save(order)
        order.items.append(LineItem("rug", 9000))
        self.assertEqual(len(self.repo.get("o-2").items), 1)

    def test_unknown_orders_raise(self):
        with self.assertRaises(OrderNotFound):
            self.repo.get("missing")
rootCause: InMemoryOrderRepository stores and returns the same Order object. The service mutates what get() returned, so the 'saved' order changes before validation has passed, and an exception leaves it half-updated. A real database returns a fresh row each time, so the repository should save and return copies.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Popping the item before raising fixes add_item only. apply_discount has the same flaw: a rejected discount is still left on the saved order, because the shared object is mutated before validation.

turns.text: When add_item rejects an order for being over the limit, the item is still in the order I read back afterwards. Why?
add_item appends the item before it validates the total, so the item is there when it raises. The simplest fix is to take the item back out before raising.
That fixes it: a rejected item is now removed before the error is raised.

transcript.verdict: The patch treats the symptom in one method. The real cause is that the repository hands out the very object it stores, so any caller that mutates and then fails has already changed the saved order. apply_discount has the identical problem, and the regression suite catches it: a rejected discount stays saved.

grading.question: Why does a failed update change data that was never saved?
grading.ideal: get() returns the stored object itself, so mutating it mutates the 'database'. Nothing separates a working copy from the saved state.

grading.question: Where is the right place to fix this, and why not in each service method?
grading.ideal: In the repository: it owns the boundary, so every caller gets safe copies. Patching each method leaves the next one broken.

grading.question: What behaviour of a real database is the in-memory repository supposed to imitate?
grading.ideal: Reads return fresh copies; changes only become visible after an explicit save.
